newsitem.title: LEBANON: Four Italians, one Irish die in Lebanon crash.
newsitem.headline: Four Italians, one Irish die in Lebanon crash.

text.p: United Nations investigators were trying on Thursday to determine the cause of a helicopter crash in which five members of the peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon died.
A U.N. officer said the dead were four Italians and one Irish soldier.

The area of the Wednesday evening crash was sealed off while investigations continued, said the officer with the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL). The helicopter crashed in the Bint Jbeil area inside Israel's occupation zone in south Lebanon.

The 4,488-member UNIFIL force was established in 1978 to restore the Lebanese government's authority over the southern part of the country after an Israeli invasion to drive out Palestinian guerrillas.

When Israel withdrew most troops following a subsequent 1982 invasion, it retained a "security zone" along the Lebanese side of the border, aided by its allies of the South Lebanon Army militia, to block attacks against northern Israel.
The U.N. force has contingents from Fiji, Finland, France, Ghana, Ireland, Italy, Nepal, Norway and Poland.
The Italian military identified their dead as Antonino Sgro, 37, Guiseppe Parisi, 33, Massimo Gatti, 35, and Daniel Forner, 35. In Dublin, the dead Irish soldier was named as Sergeant John Lynch, 34.
